caller_context.arc_paper_tool_notes: Bounded ARC paper evidence is available only through resolver-supplied typed operation requests and responses. Treat returned evidence as read-only. Do not invoke ARC CLIs, shell commands, or MCP tools from the worker. ARC and Web search are complementary discovery surfaces with no fixed order: use search-metadata or cached full-text search when suitable, and use Web search for open-world, uncached, very recent, or non-arXiv public evidence. After shortlisting an ARC-resolvable paper, deep-read it as useful through get-metadata, get-arxiv-table-of-contents, get-arxiv-section, search-arxiv-full-text, search-arxiv-equations, get-references, or get-citers. Reserve deep reads for the strongest candidates within the shared request budget. For cache-wide full-text checks, send one search-cached-full-text request whose terms array contains several concrete multiword synonyms; the CLI equivalent is repeated --term values in one call. Avoid broad single words. Terms are literal OR alternatives. A refinement response contains at most 50 paper titles, never summaries or abstracts. Record each check with its operation or query and short result.
